(c) Indebtedness secured by Liens permitted by Section 7.3(g); ... (h) guarantees made in the ordinary course of business ... in an aggregate amount outstanding at any time not to exceed the greater of (x) $50,000,000 and (y) 3.0% of Consolidated Total Assets ...; (k) Indebtedness of any Foreign Subsidiary or Foreign Subsidiary Holdco to the Parent Borrower or any other Subsidiary ...; (s) Indebtedness of the Parent Borrower and its Subsidiaries assumed in connection with Permitted Business Acquisitions or similar Investments so long as ...
findings.verifierReasoning: The r2 rule purports to represent the entire Section 7.2 prohibition and marks itself COMPLETE, but the source chapeau introduces a list of exceptions of which 7.2(e) is only one. The retrieved context already shows at least 7.2(c), 7.2(h), 7.2(k), and 7.2(s) as additional independently operative exceptions. By representing only 7.2(e) and claiming completeness, the IR would lead a reviewer to believe that no other Indebtedness is permitted under Section 7.2, which would change compliance conclusions about permitted debt. This is a material omission regardless of whether r2 was intended as scaffolding, because the COMPLETE label is not supported.

findings.sourceEvidence: Create, incur, assume or suffer to exist any Indebtedness, except:
findings.verifierReasoning: The source chapeau prohibits four distinct modes of activity: create, incur, assume, and suffer to exist. The IR reduces the prohibition to the single action label INCUR_DEBT. 'Suffer to exist' is a separate and important prohibition for already-outstanding Indebtedness, which is precisely the category addressed by the 7.2(e) exception for Closing Date debt. As rendered, the prohibition rule's action label does not on its face cover the continued existence of unauthorized debt. If the IR schema intends INCUR_DEBT as a coarse hypernym covering all debt-related prohibited acts, this may be only a labeling issue; but as written the representation is narrower than the source chapeau and could affect how the prohibition is applied.
